Against the sharp brightness of the trumpet, the trombone sounds deeper and more commanding; against the soft restraint of the French horn, it is more direct and forceful. The trombone is a brass instrument, classed as an aerophone, Hornbostel–Sachs number 423.22. The player buzzes the lips inside the mouthpiece to set the air column sounding; most trombones change pitch by moving the slide back and forth with the right hand, unlike other brass instruments, which usually use valves. The most common are the tenor trombone and the bass trombone. Its tubing is about twice the length of a trumpet's and the sound goes straight out through the bell. The trombone appears in symphony orchestras, jazz, marching bands and wind ensembles; historically it was also used at outdoor events in Europe, in concerts, ceremonies, dance bands and town and court bands, and in religious settings such as the tower watches of the German city-states and St Mark's Basilica in Venice.
